Lower the starting organic fraction from the best method while preserving its temperature and gradient slope, aiming to improve the lone under-resolved pair. The best run's 2.81-minute last peak leaves substantial room for increased retention without a time penalty.

The critical pair approached co-elution when phi0 decreased to 0.40; another step may carry it through an elution-order crossover and restore separation. Keep temperature and slope fixed to test this selectivity change, with sufficient time margin for the later peaks.

Injection 10 reached the maximum CRF, so test a modestly steeper gradient to shorten elution while retaining full resolution. Holding the solvent endpoints and temperature fixed isolates the slope response of the closest pairs.

Shortening the gradient improved the minimum resolution while preserving maximum CRF. Test a further reduction to 20 minutes at the same temperature and solvent endpoints to shorten elution and determine whether the narrowing fourth–fifth pair remains fully resolved.

Continue shortening the fully resolved method while holding temperature and solvent endpoints fixed. A 14-minute gradient tests the likely resolution boundary for the fourth–fifth pair, whose resolution decreased from 2.71 to 2.12 in the last step.

Test one grid step shorter to locate the full-resolution boundary, keeping temperature and solvent endpoints unchanged. The fourth–fifth pair is now limiting at R = 1.61; if it falls below 1.5, retain the 14-minute gradient as the shortest fully resolved method found so far.

Retain injection 13 as the fastest fully resolved method found, and test a faster-eluting alternative near injection 2. Lowering temperature by 5 °C isolates whether temperature selectivity can resolve its lone critical pair while keeping the last peak below 4.58 minutes.

Cooling worsened the critical pair, so test 5 °C above injection 2 while keeping its gradient unchanged. Warming may improve that pair and shorten elution, though the neighboring pair must be checked for lost resolution.

Test a 5 °C increase from the fastest fully resolved method, injection 13, while holding its gradient fixed. This checks whether temperature can shorten elution without sacrificing either of the closely spaced middle pairs.

Test a substantially steeper gradient from injection 2, whose only deficient pair had R = 1.08. Because this solvent window lies on the opposite side of the apparent selectivity crossover, steepening may improve that pair while further shortening the already rapid elution.

Return to the fully resolving solvent window and test cooling to counter the critical-pair compression caused by a shorter gradient. An 8-minute gradient may offset the added retention at 25 °C and produce faster full separation than injection 13.

Injection 19 is now the fastest fully resolved method found; test one grid step shorter at the same temperature and solvent endpoints. Monitor both the fourth–fifth and sixth–seventh pairs, which have little resolution margin above 1.5.

Test a lower starting organic fraction to restore selectivity for the middle pair while using a short gradient to limit retention. Returning to 30 °C may also improve the late pair that became limiting at 25 °C; injection 19 remains the fastest fully resolved fallback.

Lower temperature by one step from injection 21 to test whether cooling restores its lone under-resolved middle pair. Keep the gradient fixed and monitor the late pairs for temperature-induced compression, retaining injection 19 as the fastest fully resolved fallback.

Reduce gradient steepness from injection 21 to improve its limiting middle pair, using 30 °C to preserve late-pair separation. The lower endpoint remains above the estimated last-peak elution composition, so this should avoid a prolonged final hold.

Trim injection 19’s unused gradient tail while preserving its initial composition, temperature, and slope of 0.05 organic fraction per minute. Its last peak eluted at an estimated organic fraction of 0.525, below the new endpoint, so full resolution should be retained with a shorter programmed gradient.

Use the final injection to test a finer steepness increase, from 0.050 to 0.055 organic fraction per minute, between the successful and over-compressed slopes. This may shorten elution while retaining full resolution; injection 24 remains the maximum-CRF fallback if either critical pair drops below 1.5.
